overview: Rome's civil wars left Julius Caesar's adopted heir Octavian in control after he defeated Mark Antony and Cleopatra. In **27 BC**, he presented a settlement as a restoration of authority to the Senate and Roman people while retaining command of provinces that held most of the army. The Senate gave him the name **Augustus**. The settlement marks the conventional beginning of the Principate, Augustus’s new regime, which retained institutions inherited from the Republic.

keyMoments.title: Actium and the conquest of Egypt
keyMoments.text: In 31 BC, **Octavian's fleet**, led by Marcus Agrippa, defeated **Mark Antony and Cleopatra** at the **Battle of Actium** off western Greece. Antony and Cleopatra returned to Egypt. The war ended the following year after Octavian invaded Egypt and both took their own lives.

keyMoments.title: The census of 28 BC
keyMoments.text: Octavian shared the consulship with **Agrippa** in 28 BC, when a **census of Roman citizens** was taken. In his own account, Octavian says he performed the purification ceremony that went with it, the first in forty-one years. According to Cassius Dio, Octavian was also made **princeps senatus**, the Senate’s first-ranking member, and revoked regulations dating from the triumvirate.

keyMoments.title: The Republic 'restored'
keyMoments.text: In **January 27 BC**, Octavian presented his settlement as a transfer of authority to the **Senate and Roman people**. He received a ten-year command over a group of provinces containing most of the army, including Syria, Gaul and parts of Spain. The Senate also gave him the name **Augustus**. He kept decisive military power while presenting his rule in republican terms.

keyMoments.title: Power without the consulship
keyMoments.text: In **23 BC**, Augustus gave up his regular hold on the **consulship** and took on **tribunician power**. According to the historian Cassius Dio, Augustus also received command superior to that of provincial governors. Historians debate whether that superior command dates to this settlement. Augustus could now exercise tribunician authority while leaving the consulship open to others.

deepFacts.text: The ancient biographer **Suetonius** says that some proposed naming Octavian **Romulus**, after Rome's legendary founder. The historian **Cassius Dio** says Octavian himself favoured the name but abandoned it because it suggested kingship. The Senate instead gave him the honorific **Augustus**, a name with religious associations.

The Roman month **Sextilis** was renamed **Augustus**, the source of the English name August. Sextilis meant sixth, reflecting the Roman tradition of counting March as the first month. The month followed July, which had already been named for Julius Caesar.

Augustus's building programme reshaped Rome. He records that he built the **Forum of Augustus** and that the Senate decreed the **Ara Pacis**, or Altar of Augustan Peace, in honour of his return from Spain and Gaul.
